page: Microsoft Azure M32ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization via Intel VMX, hyper-threading, and instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The server is equipped with 875.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory density of 27.34 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a 1049 GB SSD and is Premium Storage capable. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is consistently positioned in the bottom 10%, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core CPU (1038.69), Geekbench single-core (896.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (17.25 GB/sec). Conversely, multi-core and parallelized workloads achieve average performance in the middle 50% tier, including stress-ng multi-core CPU (21896.23), Geekbench multi-core (8259.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (99.51 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, reaching 1220.83 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 91.77 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though the Passmark memory score falls into the weak bottom 25% category.

Given the massive memory allocation relative to compute resources, this server is designed for memory-intensive workloads. Database operations perform in the average tier with 8081.75 Passmark database operations and 20.43 million operations per second on Redis SET. It is suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise applications, and data caching layers where memory capacity is the primary constraint rather than raw single-threaded CPU speed.

It features an exceptionally high memory capacity of 875.0 GB (27.34 GB per core) and includes 1049 GB of local SSD storage. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supports AVX-512F and AES instructions. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core operations, database tasks, and Redis SET operations (20.43 million operations/sec) maintain average performance within the middle 50% tier. This resource profile makes the M32ms highly suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale caching, and database operations where memory capacity is prioritized over high single-threaded compute speeds.
